text:
maya: Quick Q — I was on a 10-week short-term secondment to the UK (2024-05-06 → 2024-07-15). I'm planning to take parental leave starting 2024-09-02. Does my leave eligibility or company top-up get prorated because of the assignment? Also do I need to submit separate paperwork for the UK period?
chris: cc @emma (my manager). @maya we'll need HR to confirm but my understanding is continuous service still counts. tagging People Ops to confirm pay/proration/any paperwork.
emma: Hi @maya — short answer: your continuous service with Redwood counts toward parental leave eligibility. The nuance is how pay is calculated: statutory and company top-up depend on which payroll paid you during the secondment and any local statutory rules. Can you share 1) exact secondment dates, 2) which payroll paid you while on assignment, and 3) whether you received any one-off/bonus payments during that time? I'll DM the checklist. Our internal guidance: https://redwood.internal/hr/leave#international-secondments
maya: thanks — posting details: secondment dates 2024-05-06 to 2024-07-15. Paid via US payroll (host expenses routed through host team). Visa sponsored by host. Benefits stayed active. No bonuses during that window. Planning leave start 2024-09-02.
emma: Got it — because you remained on US payroll and benefits were continuous, eligibility (qualifying service) is unaffected. Payroll will still calculate statutory pay based on earnings; company top-up eligibility remains. We do need paperwork so we can record the secondment in HR records and compute earnings correctly. Please complete the parental leave intent form and attach: secondment dates, a payslip covering the assignment month, and planned leave start date. Form: https://redwood.internal/hr/forms/parental-leave-intent
sam-payroll: @maya from payroll: important note — we only prorate company-paid leave if someone had an unpaid leave or break in service. Since you were paid, there should be no proration to eligibility. For pay amount we use average earnings over the statutory reference period (US policy uses the last 8 weeks). If you want to sanity-check, you can run a quick calc: `avg_weekly_pay = sum(earnings_last_8_weeks) / 8`. If any host reimbursements were recorded as expense (not wages), they may be excluded from that sum — please attach payslip so payroll can verify.
emma: Also reminder: People Ops needs minimum 30 days notice for standard parental leave paperwork. You're within that window, so please submit ASAP. We'll issue the formal leave confirmation letter and return-to-work instructions once payroll verifies the pay calculation.
HRBot: Checklist generated for maya: 1) Submit parental leave intent form (link above). 2) Attach proof of secondment dates and payslip. 3) Confirm planned leave start date. 4) Payroll will run pre-check and confirm statutory pay basis. 5) People Ops will send official leave confirmation and manager guidance. Tracker ID: HR-PL-2024-8742 (for internal use).
maya: Perfect — I'll submit today and upload the payslip. One small follow-up: do I need to separately notify the UK host team about coverage/handovers?
chris: I'll take that on — will coordinate coverage with the UK host leads and post a handover plan in the team's channel. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks everyone, really helpful. If payroll or People Ops need anything else I'll ping here or DM.
